intent.raw_query: Nepal trekking Annapurna, $2000 solo, October 2026, 14 days

experiences.name: Annapurna Base Camp Trek
experiences.description: Embark on the iconic multi-day trek to Annapurna Base Camp at 4,130m, passing through rhododendron forests, traditional Gurung villages, and dramatic mountain landscapes with stunning views of Annapurna I, Machapuchare, and Hiunchuli peaks.

experiences.name: Poon Hill Sunrise Hike
experiences.description: Rise before dawn and hike to Poon Hill viewpoint at 3,210m for one of Nepal's most celebrated panoramic Himalayan sunrises, with golden light illuminating the Annapurna and Dhaulagiri ranges in a breathtaking 180-degree spectacle.

experiences.name: Gurung Village Cultural Homestay
experiences.description: Stay overnight in a traditional Gurung ethnic village, sharing meals of dal bhat and local millet raksi with host families, learning about ancient shamanic Bon-Buddhist traditions, and experiencing authentic mountain community life far from tourist trails.

experiences.name: Mardi Himal Trek
experiences.description: Explore the lesser-known Mardi Himal trail, a hidden gem offering solitude through dense bamboo and rhododendron forests, alpine meadows, and a high camp at 4,500m with jaw-dropping close-up views of Machapuchare (Fishtail Mountain) without the crowds of main routes.
experiences.location: Mardi Himal, Eastern Annapurna Conservation Area

experiences.name: Jhinu Danda Natural Hot Springs Soak
experiences.description: Descend to the natural riverside hot springs along the Modi Khola river, a perfect reward after days of trekking. Soak in geothermal mineral pools surrounded by lush jungle while listening to the rushing glacial river, relieving tired muscles in a stunning natural setting.
experiences.location: Jhinu Danda, Modi Khola River Valley

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Annapurna, Nepal
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery — flight arrives at 22:30, so no morning activities scheduled
day_by_day.afternoon: Rest and recovery — flight arrives at 22:30, so no afternoon activities scheduled
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Tribhuvan International Airport, Kathmandu at 22:30. Clear immigration, collect baggage, and arrange a pre-booked budget taxi or shared shuttle to your accommodation near the Annapurna region (or overnight in Kathmandu if needed). Check in, freshen up, and rest.

meals.breakfast: On the plane
meals.lunch: On the plane or airport snacks
meals.dinner: Quick dal bhat or momos from a local late-night eatery near the airport (~300–400 NPR)

day_by_day.notes: Since the flight lands late at night, Day 1 is purely arrival and rest. If the journey to Pokhara (gateway to Annapurna) is not completed tonight, plan an early morning bus or flight on Day 2. Keep energy drinks and light snacks handy for the transfer.

day_by_day.morning: Take an early morning tourist bus or local bus from Kathmandu to Pokhara (approximately 6–7 hours, ~800–1,200 NPR). Enjoy scenic mountain views along the Prithvi Highway. Arrive in Pokhara by early afternoon.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to budget guesthouse in Lakeside, Pokhara. Stroll along Phewa Lake promenade, visit the local market in Lakeside (Baidam) to pick up any last-minute trekking supplies at budget prices. Visit the trekking permit office to obtain TIMS card (~2,000 NPR) and Annapurna Conservation Area Permit/ACAP (~3,000 NPR).
day_by_day.evening: Walk along Phewa Lakeside at sunset. Explore Lakeside's budget restaurants and cafes. Prepare trekking gear and pack your bag for the trail starting tomorrow.

meals.breakfast: Simple bread, egg, and tea at a Kathmandu tea house before departure (~150–200 NPR)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or roadside dhaba meal during bus journey (~200–300 NPR)
meals.dinner: Dal bhat set meal at a local Lakeside restaurant (~400–600 NPR)

day_by_day.notes: Obtain your TIMS card and ACAP permit today — these are mandatory for trekking in the Annapurna region. Budget guesthouses in Lakeside, Pokhara cost around 500–800 NPR per night. Confirm your trekking route (Annapurna Base Camp or Poon Hill circuit) and book a guide if desired.

day_by_day.morning: Take a local bus or taxi from Pokhara to Nayapul (approximately 1.5 hours, ~200–300 NPR by local bus). Begin the trek from Nayapul, crossing the Modi Khola river and walking through terraced rice fields and small villages toward Tikhedhunga (approximately 3–4 hours trekking, moderate trail).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue trekking from Tikhedhunga up the famous stone staircase to Ulleri (approximately 1.5–2 hours, steep ascent with over 3,000 stone steps). Enjoy panoramic views of the Annapurna South and Hiunchuli peaks. Arrive at Ulleri and check in to a basic teahouse (~300–500 NPR per night).
day_by_day.evening: Relax on the teahouse terrace with views of the mountains. Chat with fellow trekkers, stretch tired muscles, and enjoy the peaceful Himalayan village atmosphere. Early bedtime to prepare for Day 4.

meals.breakfast: Porridge or egg toast at Lakeside guesthouse before departure (~200–300 NPR)
meals.lunch: Dal bhat or noodle soup at a teahouse in Tikhedhunga (~400–500 NPR)
meals.dinner: Dal bhat set meal at Ulleri teahouse (~500–600 NPR)

day_by_day.notes: October is peak trekking season — trails will be busy but weather is typically clear and dry, ideal for mountain views. Carry at least 2 liters of water. The stone staircase to Ulleri is strenuous; take it slow and steady. Teahouse accommodation is basic but comfortable — shared bathrooms are standard.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning start from Ulleri. Trek through dense rhododendron and oak forests toward Ghorepani (approximately 3–4 hours, gradual ascent). The forest trail is magical in October with clear skies and colorful foliage. Arrive at Ghorepani (2,874m) by late morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to a budget teahouse in Ghorepani (~400–600 NPR). Rest and acclimatize to the altitude. Take a short afternoon walk around the village and explore the local market stalls selling handicrafts and warm gear.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset walk to Poon Hill viewpoint (30-minute uphill walk from Ghorepani). Enjoy breathtaking panoramic views of Dhaulagiri, Annapurna I, Annapurna South, Machapuchare (Fishtail), and Hiunchuli in the golden evening light. Return to teahouse for dinner and rest.

meals.breakfast: Porridge with honey and tea at Ulleri teahouse (~300–400 NPR)
meals.lunch: Vegetable fried rice or thukpa soup at a trail teahouse (~400–500 NPR)
meals.dinner: Dal bhat or pasta at Ghorepani teahouse (~500–700 NPR)

day_by_day.notes: Ghorepani sits at 2,874m — some trekkers feel mild altitude effects (headache, fatigue). Stay hydrated and avoid alcohol. Set an alarm for 04:30 tomorrow for the famous Poon Hill sunrise. Temperatures drop significantly at night — have a warm sleeping bag or rent blankets from the teahouse (~100–150 NPR).

day_by_day.morning: Wake up at 04:30 and hike to Poon Hill (3,210m) for the iconic sunrise over the Annapurna and Dhaulagiri ranges (approximately 45 minutes uphill). Watch the golden alpenglow illuminate Dhaulagiri (8,167m), Annapurna I (8,091m), and Machapuchare (6,993m). Return to Ghorepani for breakfast. Then trek onward through rhododendron forests to Tadapani (approximately 4–5 hours).
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Tadapani (2,630m). Check in to a teahouse and enjoy lunch with mountain views. Rest your legs and explore the small hilltop village. Optional short nature walk through the surrounding forest to spot Himalayan birds and wildlife.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy the peaceful atmosphere of Tadapani village. Watch the evening alpenglow on Annapurna South and Machapuchare from the teahouse terrace. Early dinner and rest.

meals.breakfast: Hot porridge, boiled eggs, and milk tea at Ghorepani teahouse after sunrise (~300–400 NPR)
meals.lunch: Vegetable soup and chapati at Tadapani teahouse (~400–500 NPR)
meals.dinner: Dal bhat set meal at Tadapani teahouse (~500–600 NPR)

day_by_day.notes: The Poon Hill sunrise is one of the most spectacular experiences in the Annapurna region — do not miss it! Carry a headlamp for the pre-dawn hike. The trail from Ghorepani to Tadapani passes through stunning rhododendron forest. In October, rhododendrons are not in bloom but the forest is lush and green.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Tadapani down through forest and terraced farmland to Chhomrong (2,170m), a major village on the Annapurna Base Camp route (approximately 4–5 hours). The trail offers spectacular close-up views of Annapurna South and Machapuchare throughout the descent.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Chhomrong. Check in to a budget teahouse (~400–600 NPR). Explore this large, well-equipped village — it has bakeries, internet cafes, and well-stocked shops. Stock up on snacks, chocolates, and supplies for the higher altitude sections ahead where prices increase.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a relaxed evening in Chhomrong. Visit the Chhomrong Cottage bakery for fresh apple pie or cinnamon rolls (a trekker favorite). Watch the sunset over Annapurna South towering directly above the village.

meals.breakfast: Pancakes with honey and tea at Tadapani teahouse (~300–400 NPR)
meals.lunch: Fried noodles or egg fried rice at a trail teahouse (~400–500 NPR)
meals.dinner: Dal bhat or pizza at a Chhomrong teahouse (~500–700 NPR)

day_by_day.notes: Chhomrong is the last major resupply point before Annapurna Base Camp. Buy extra snacks, energy bars, and water purification tablets here as prices at higher teahouses can be 2–3x more expensive. Charge all electronic devices — reliable electricity becomes less available higher up.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Chhomrong down stone steps to Sinuwa and continue through bamboo and rhododendron forest to Bamboo (2,310m) and onward to Dovan (2,600m) (approximately 4–5 hours total). The trail follows the Modi Khola river valley, gradually ascending into the Annapurna Sanctuary.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue trekking from Dovan to Himalaya Hotel (2,920m) or push on to Deurali (3,230m) if energy permits (approximately 2–3 more hours). The landscape becomes increasingly dramatic as you enter the glacial valley. Check in to a teahouse and rest.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy the incredible high-altitude ambiance. The walls of Annapurna South, Hiunchuli, and Machapuchare tower on all sides. Stargazing from the teahouse terrace on a clear October night can be extraordinary. Early bedtime for acclimatization.

meals.breakfast: Muesli with hot milk and tea at Chhomrong teahouse (~300–400 NPR)
meals.lunch: Dal bhat or instant noodles at Bamboo or Dovan teahouse (~500–700 NPR — prices increase with altitude)
meals.dinner: Dal bhat set meal at Himalaya Hotel or Deurali teahouse (~600–800 NPR)

day_by_day.notes: The trail between Chhomrong and Deurali passes through avalanche-prone areas — always check with teahouse owners about current trail conditions. In October, conditions are generally stable but remain alert. Altitude increases significantly — watch for symptoms of Acute Mountain Sickness (AMS): headache, nausea, dizziness. Ascend slowly.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning start from Deurali or Himalaya Hotel. Trek through the dramatic glacial moraine landscape to Machhapuchhre Base Camp/MBC (3,700m) (approximately 2–3 hours). The trail offers stunning views of Machapuchare's iconic fishtail peak directly ahead. Arrive at MBC and take a rest break.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the final push from MBC to Annapurna Base Camp/ABC (4,130m) (approximately 2 hours). The trail crosses open glacial terrain with views of Annapurna I, Annapurna South, Gangapurna, Glacier Dome, and Hiunchuli forming a complete 360-degree amphitheater of giants. Arrive at ABC — a profound achievement!
day_by_day.evening: Watch the sunset alpenglow paint the surrounding 7,000–8,000m peaks in shades of orange, pink, and gold from Annapurna Base Camp. Check in to a teahouse at ABC (~600–800 NPR). Celebrate reaching base camp with fellow trekkers. Early rest — it will be very cold tonight (temperatures can drop to -10°C or below).

meals.breakfast: Porridge and hot lemon tea at Deurali teahouse (~400–500 NPR)
meals.lunch: Soup and bread at Machhapuchhre Base Camp (~600–800 NPR)
meals.dinner: Dal bhat or garlic soup with pasta at Annapurna Base Camp teahouse (~700–900 NPR)

day_by_day.notes: Reaching Annapurna Base Camp at 4,130m is the highlight of the trek! October offers some of the best clear weather windows. Drink plenty of fluids, avoid alcohol, and eat well. Temperatures at ABC can be bitterly cold at night — ensure you have adequate warm layers, a good sleeping bag, and warm gloves. Sunrise from ABC is absolutely spectacular.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up before sunrise (approximately 05:30) to witness the incredible golden sunrise over the Annapurna massif from base camp. The peaks glow dramatically in the early morning light — one of the most awe-inspiring sights in the Himalayas. Spend the morning exploring the base camp area and soaking in the 360-degree mountain panorama.
day_by_day.afternoon: Begin the descent from Annapurna Base Camp back to Machhapuchhre Base Camp and continue down to Bamboo (2,310m) (approximately 5–6 hours descent). The descent is faster but tough on the knees — use trekking poles if available.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Bamboo teahouse, tired but elated. Enjoy a well-deserved hot meal and rest. Reflect on the incredible achievement of reaching ABC.

meals.breakfast: Hot porridge and sweet milk tea at ABC teahouse (~400–500 NPR)
meals.lunch: Instant noodles or soup at MBC (~600–700 NPR)
meals.dinner: Dal bhat set meal at Bamboo teahouse (~500–600 NPR)

day_by_day.notes: The descent from ABC to Bamboo is long (approximately 1,820m elevation loss). Pace yourself, protect your knees, and take regular breaks. Bamboo teahouses are basic but welcoming after a long day. Your legs will be very tired — stretch thoroughly before sleep to avoid muscle cramps.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Bamboo back up to Chhomrong (approximately 3–4 hours). The ascent from Sinuwa back up to Chhomrong involves a steep stone staircase — take it slowly. Arrive at Chhomrong for a well-deserved rest.
day_by_day.afternoon: Enjoy a relaxed afternoon in Chhomrong. Visit the famous Chhomrong Cottage for apple pie and coffee. Optional: soak tired feet in cold mountain stream water. Do laundry if needed (laundry services available ~200–300 NPR). Restock on snacks for remaining trek days.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a leisurely dinner in Chhomrong. Watch the evening light fade over Annapurna South. Chat with other trekkers about their ABC experiences. Early rest to prepare for the next section.

meals.breakfast: Pancakes or muesli at Bamboo teahouse (~400–500 NPR)
meals.lunch: Dal bhat or pasta at a trail teahouse (~500–600 NPR)
meals.dinner: Pizza or dal bhat at Chhomrong teahouse (~500–700 NPR)

day_by_day.notes: Chhomrong is a great place to rest and recover after the demanding ABC section. If your knees are sore, consider purchasing a bamboo trekking stick from a local shop (~100–200 NPR). Check weather forecasts for the remaining trek days.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Chhomrong back toward Ghorepani via Tadapani (approximately 5–6 hours). This section retraces part of the earlier route through beautiful rhododendron and oak forest. Enjoy the familiar but always stunning mountain views of Annapurna South and Machapuchare.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Ghorepani (2,874m). Check in to a teahouse and rest. Optional afternoon hike to Poon Hill again for a second chance at the panoramic views in the afternoon light — the perspective differs beautifully from the morning visit.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening in Ghorepani. Enjoy a hearty meal and celebrate the near-completion of the trek. The village has a lively atmosphere with trekkers from all over the world.

meals.breakfast: Porridge and boiled eggs at Chhomrong teahouse (~300–400 NPR)
meals.lunch: Vegetable soup and chapati at Tadapani teahouse (~400–500 NPR)
meals.dinner: Dal bhat set meal at Ghorepani teahouse (~500–600 NPR)

day_by_day.notes: If you want a second Poon Hill sunrise tomorrow morning, set your alarm for 04:30 again. The trail between Tadapani and Ghorepani is well-marked but can be muddy after rain — wear proper trekking boots. October weather is generally dry but afternoon clouds are common.

day_by_day.morning: Optional second Poon Hill sunrise (04:30 start) for a final farewell view of the Annapurna and Dhaulagiri ranges. Return to Ghorepani for breakfast. Then begin the descent through rhododendron forest toward Ulleri and down to Tikhedhunga (approximately 4–5 hours). The descent through the stone staircase from Ulleri is steep — take care.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue trekking from Tikhedhunga to Nayapul (approximately 1.5–2 hours on a relatively flat trail along the Modi Khola river). Arrive at Nayapul and take a local bus or jeep back to Pokhara (approximately 1.5 hours, ~200–300 NPR).
day_by_day.evening: Arrive back in Pokhara — Lakeside area. Check in to a budget guesthouse (~500–800 NPR). Celebrate completing the Annapurna Base Camp trek! Enjoy a proper hot shower, do laundry, and treat yourself to a nicer dinner to celebrate.

meals.breakfast: Hot porridge and milk tea at Ghorepani teahouse after sunrise (~300–400 NPR)
meals.lunch: Dal bhat at a Tikhedhunga teahouse (~400–500 NPR)
meals.dinner: Celebration dinner at a Lakeside restaurant — try traditional Nepali thali or continental food (~600–1,000 NPR as a treat)

day_by_day.notes: You have completed the Annapurna Base Camp trek! This is a major achievement. Pokhara has excellent budget massage parlors offering foot and body massages (~500–800 NPR per hour) — highly recommended after 10 days of trekking. Lakeside has ATMs, pharmacies, and gear shops if you need anything.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery day in Pokhara. Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely breakfast at a Lakeside cafe. Rent a rowboat on Phewa Lake (~500–600 NPR per hour) and row to the Tal Barahi Temple on the island in the middle of the lake — a beautiful Hindu temple accessible only by boat.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the International Mountain Museum in Pokhara (entry ~400 NPR) — a fascinating museum dedicated to the history of Himalayan mountaineering, featuring exhibits on Annapurna, Everest, and other 8,000m peaks. Alternatively, hike up to the World Peace Pagoda (Shanti Stupa) for panoramic views of Pokhara, Phewa Lake, and the Annapurna range (free entry, ~45-minute uphill walk or taxi for ~300 NPR).
day_by_day.evening: Explore Lakeside's vibrant evening market. Browse souvenir shops for budget-friendly gifts: Tibetan singing bowls, thangka paintings, pashmina scarves, and trekking keepsakes. Enjoy a farewell dinner at a lakeside restaurant with mountain views.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast (eggs, toast, juice, coffee) at a Lakeside cafe (~400–600 NPR)
meals.lunch: Momo (dumplings) and lassi at a local Pokhara restaurant (~300–400 NPR)
meals.dinner: Nepali set dinner (thali) with live traditional music at a cultural restaurant (~700–1,000 NPR)

day_by_day.notes: Pokhara is a wonderful city to relax and recover in after the trek. The World Peace Pagoda offers one of the best views in Pokhara — go at sunset for the best light on the Annapurna range. If budget allows, a 30-minute ultralight aircraft or paragliding flight over Pokhara and the Himalayas is an unforgettable experience (~5,000–8,000 NPR for paragliding).

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Pokhara. Wake up early for a last sunrise view of the Annapurna range reflected in Phewa Lake — a perfect final memory. Pack your bags and check out of the guesthouse. Take a local bus or tourist bus back to Kathmandu (approximately 6–7 hours, ~800–1,200 NPR) or book a short domestic flight (~4,000–6,000 NPR, 25 minutes) if budget allows for the convenience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Kathmandu. Check in to a budget guesthouse in Thamel (~600–1,000 NPR). Explore Thamel's famous bazaar for last-minute souvenir shopping: handicrafts, spices, Nepali tea, thangka art, and trekking gear. Visit Pashupatinath Temple or Boudhanath Stupa if time permits (Boudhanath entry ~400 NPR).
day_by_day.evening: Final dinner in Kathmandu at a Thamel restaurant. Reflect on 14 incredible days exploring the Annapurna region. Pack for your departure flight and prepare all travel documents. Get a good night's rest before heading to the airport.

meals.breakfast: Final Nepali breakfast — sel roti (rice flour donuts) with tea at a local Pokhara bakery (~200–300 NPR)
meals.lunch: Dal bhat or snacks during the bus journey (~300–400 NPR)
meals.dinner: Final Nepali dinner in Thamel — try traditional Newari cuisine or a classic dal bhat at a local restaurant (~500–800 NPR)

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before your departure flight for airport check-in and security at Tribhuvan International Airport. Keep all trekking permits and receipts as souvenirs — they make wonderful mementos. Budget summary estimate for the full 14-day trip: Permits (TIMS + ACAP) ~5,000 NPR, accommodation ~8,000–12,000 NPR total, food ~15,000–20,000 NPR total, transport ~5,000–7,000 NPR total. Total estimated budget: ~33,000–44,000 NPR (~$250–$330 USD) excluding international flights.

trip_options.title: Classic Annapurna, Nepal Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery — flight arrives at 22:30, so no morning activities scheduled
day_by_day.afternoon: Rest and recovery — flight arrives at 22:30, so no afternoon activities scheduled
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Tribhuvan International Airport, Kathmandu at 22:30. Clear immigration, collect luggage, and meet your pre-arranged transfer. Drive to your accommodation near the Annapurna region (or overnight in Kathmandu/Pokhara depending on transfer logistics). Check in to Aegean Bliss Resort and settle in for the night.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in-flight meal
meals.lunch: N/A — in-flight meal
meals.dinner: Light snack or dal bhat available at the resort upon late arrival if arranged in advance

day_by_day.notes: Confirm airport transfer in advance. Keep a change of clothes and essentials in your carry-on for a comfortable first night. Hydrate well — altitude acclimatization begins here.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the resort. Spend the morning orienting yourself — walk the resort grounds, breathe in the Himalayan air, and get acquainted with the Annapurna surroundings. Visit the resort's viewpoint for your first panoramic views of the Annapurna massif.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a short, easy introductory hike around the immediate resort area and nearby village trails. Explore the local village on foot, observe daily Nepali life, and visit a small local monastery or chorten (Buddhist shrine) if nearby. This gentle walk helps with initial acclimatization.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a relaxed dinner at the resort restaurant. Attend a brief orientation session if offered by the resort or your guide about the upcoming trekking days. Rest early to recover from jet lag.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort — try local items like sel roti (rice doughnuts), eggs, and Nepali tea or coffee
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the resort or a nearby teahouse — try vegetable soup and chapati
meals.dinner: Dal bhat (lentil soup, rice, vegetables, and pickle) at the resort restaurant — the quintessential Nepali meal, approximately NPR 400–600

day_by_day.notes: Do not over-exert on Day 2. Acclimatization is critical. Drink at least 3–4 liters of water. Avoid alcohol for the first couple of days.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning sunrise viewing from a nearby viewpoint (ask resort staff for the best local spot). After sunrise, enjoy breakfast and prepare for a half-day guided nature walk through rhododendron and oak forests in the lower Annapurna foothills. Look out for Himalayan birds like the Danphe (Impeyan pheasant, Nepal's national bird).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Pokhara city (if the resort is near Pokhara) — explore the Phewa Lake shoreline, stroll the lakeside promenade, and browse local trekking gear shops on Lakeside Road. Alternatively, visit a local organic farm or tea garden near the resort for a nature-immersive experience.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset boat ride on Phewa Lake with views of the Annapurna and Machhapuchhre (Fishtail) reflections on the lake. Return to the resort for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Porridge with honey and fresh fruit, toast, and masala tea at the resort
meals.lunch: Momos (Nepali dumplings) and thukpa (noodle soup) at a local teahouse in Pokhara Lakeside — approximately NPR 300–500
meals.dinner: Grilled local trout or vegetable curry with rice at a mid-range lakeside restaurant — approximately NPR 600–900

day_by_day.notes: Boat rental on Phewa Lake costs approximately NPR 500–800 per hour. Bring sunscreen and a light jacket for the evening. October weather in Annapurna is typically clear and cool — ideal trekking season.

day_by_day.morning: Begin the classic Annapurna Circuit or Annapurna Base Camp (ABC) approach trek. Start from Nayapul or Kande (accessible by jeep/bus from Pokhara, approximately 1.5 hours). Begin trekking through terraced rice fields, suspension bridges, and riverside trails toward Tikhedhunga or Ghandruk. Morning trek duration: 3–4 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Ghandruk village — one of the largest Gurung villages in Nepal. Explore the Gurung Museum to learn about the indigenous Gurung culture, traditions, and history. Visit the local gompa (Buddhist monastery). Rest and enjoy the stunning views of Annapurna South and Hiunchuli.
day_by_day.evening: Check in to a mid-range teahouse in Ghandruk (approximately NPR 500–800 per night for a twin room). Socialize with fellow trekkers over dinner. Enjoy the crisp mountain evening air.

meals.breakfast: Pancakes with honey and tea at the resort before departure
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or stop at a trail teahouse — try egg fried rice or noodle soup — approximately NPR 300–500
meals.dinner: Dal bhat at Ghandruk teahouse — unlimited refills customary — approximately NPR 500–700

day_by_day.notes: Ghandruk sits at approximately 1,940m elevation. Trek distance from Nayapul to Ghandruk is approximately 8–10 km. Trekking permits required: ACAP (Annapurna Conservation Area Permit) and TIMS card — arrange in Pokhara the day before if not already done.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early (5:30–6:00 AM) for spectacular sunrise views over Annapurna South, Hiunchuli, and Machhapuchhre from Ghandruk. After breakfast, continue trekking toward Chhomrong — the gateway village to the Annapurna Sanctuary. The trail involves a descent and steep ascent through rhododendron forests. Trek duration: 4–5 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Chhomrong (2,170m). Explore this picturesque Gurung village perched on a hillside. Visit the local school and small monastery. Enjoy sweeping views of the Annapurna massif from the village terraces.
day_by_day.evening: Rest at a comfortable teahouse in Chhomrong. Enjoy a warm shower (solar-heated, available at most teahouses for a small fee). Stretch and treat any sore muscles. Early bedtime to prepare for the next day's trek.

meals.breakfast: Oatmeal porridge, boiled eggs, and Nepali black tea at Ghandruk teahouse
meals.lunch: Vegetable soup and chapati at a trail teahouse between Ghandruk and Chhomrong
meals.dinner: Garlic soup (highly recommended for altitude), dal bhat or pasta at Chhomrong teahouse — approximately NPR 500–700

day_by_day.notes: Garlic soup is a popular natural remedy for altitude sickness on the trail — highly recommended. Chhomrong has reliable Wi-Fi at most teahouses (small fee). Stock up on snacks and water purification tablets here as prices increase higher up the trail.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Chhomrong early and trek through bamboo and rhododendron forests toward Himalaya Hotel (2,920m). The trail descends to the Modi Khola river and then climbs steeply. Pass through Sinuwa and Bamboo en route. Trek duration: 5–6 hours total for the day.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue trekking from Himalaya Hotel toward Dovan (2,600m) or push further to Deurali (3,230m) depending on group pace and energy. The trail becomes increasingly dramatic with towering canyon walls and the roar of the Modi Khola river. Spot mountain flora including giant balsam and high-altitude mosses.
day_by_day.evening: Check in to a teahouse at Dovan or Deurali. The environment becomes noticeably colder and more remote. Enjoy a hot dinner and rest. The night sky at this elevation is extraordinary — look for the Milky Way on a clear October night.

meals.breakfast: Tibetan bread with jam and butter, hot lemon tea at Chhomrong
meals.lunch: Noodle soup or fried rice at Sinuwa or Bamboo teahouse — approximately NPR 400–600
meals.dinner: Dal bhat with extra vegetable curry at Dovan/Deurali teahouse — approximately NPR 600–800

day_by_day.notes: The trail between Chhomrong and Deurali is heavily forested and can be slippery — trekking poles strongly recommended. Temperature drops significantly after Himalaya Hotel. Layer up with a fleece and waterproof jacket. Altitude increases rapidly — watch for any symptoms of AMS (Acute Mountain Sickness).

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Deurali to Machhapuchhre Base Camp (MBC) at 3,700m — one of the most dramatic sections of the route. The trail enters the Annapurna Sanctuary, an enclosed glacial amphitheater surrounded by eight peaks over 6,000m. The landscape transforms into a high-altitude alpine zone. Trek duration to MBC: 3–4 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: After a brief rest and lunch at MBC, continue the final push to Annapurna Base Camp (ABC) at 4,130m — approximately 2 more hours. Arrive at ABC and take in the overwhelming 360-degree panorama of Annapurna I (8,091m), Annapurna South, Hiunchuli, Gangapurna, and Machhapuchhre. This is the crown jewel of the trek.
day_by_day.evening: Celebrate reaching ABC with fellow trekkers. Watch the alpenglow — the golden-pink light that illuminates the surrounding peaks at sunset. Check in to a teahouse at ABC. The temperature will be well below freezing at night — dress in full down layers. Rest and hydrate aggressively.

meals.breakfast: Porridge and hot chocolate at Deurali — fuel up for the big day
meals.lunch: Hot soup and snacks at Machhapuchhre Base Camp teahouse
meals.dinner: Dal bhat or pasta with hot ginger lemon honey tea at ABC teahouse — approximately NPR 700–1,000 (prices are higher at altitude)

day_by_day.notes: ABC is at 4,130m — altitude sickness is a real risk. Move slowly, breathe deeply, and descend immediately if symptoms of severe AMS appear (severe headache, vomiting, loss of coordination). Teahouse rooms at ABC are basic but functional. Sleeping bag rated to -10°C strongly recommended. This is the highlight of the entire trip.

day_by_day.morning: Wake before dawn (4:30–5:00 AM) for the most spectacular sunrise of your life — watching the first golden light strike Annapurna I and the surrounding peaks from ABC. This is a once-in-a-lifetime moment. Take photographs, meditate, or simply absorb the experience in silence.
day_by_day.afternoon: Begin the descent from ABC back toward Bamboo or Sinuwa. Descending is faster but harder on the knees — take your time and use trekking poles. The familiar landscapes feel different on the way down. Arrive at Bamboo (2,310m) for the night — a significant descent that aids acclimatization recovery.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy the warmer temperatures at lower elevation. Celebrate the successful ABC summit with a well-earned hot meal. Rest your legs and reflect on the incredible journey. The bamboo forest around the teahouse is magical in the evening light.

meals.breakfast: Hot porridge and tea at ABC before sunrise — essential for warmth
meals.lunch: Packed snacks or quick stop at Himalaya Hotel on the descent
meals.dinner: Dal bhat with extra portions at Bamboo teahouse — your body needs the calories — approximately NPR 500–700

day_by_day.notes: The descent from ABC to Bamboo is approximately 12–14 km and takes 5–7 hours. Knee pain is common on descent — consider knee support bandages. Drink plenty of water. Celebrate but don't overdo it — there are still several trekking days ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Continue descent from Bamboo through Chhomrong and back toward Jhinu Danda (1,780m). Jhinu Danda is famous for its natural hot springs situated on the banks of the Modi Khola river — a perfect reward after days of strenuous trekking. Trek duration: 4–5 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Soak in the Jhinu Danda natural hot springs — a blissful, therapeutic experience for tired trekking muscles. The hot springs are set in a gorgeous riverside location with jungle surroundings. Spend 1–2 hours relaxing and unwinding. This is one of the most rewarding experiences on the Annapurna trail.
day_by_day.evening: Check in to a teahouse in Jhinu Danda or New Bridge. Enjoy a relaxed evening — the hardest trekking is now behind you. Watch the stars from the riverside. Sleep deeply.

meals.breakfast: Pancakes and tea at Bamboo teahouse
meals.lunch: Vegetable soup and bread at a trail teahouse near Chhomrong
meals.dinner: Grilled vegetables with rice and lentil soup at Jhinu Danda teahouse — approximately NPR 500–700

day_by_day.notes: Hot springs entry fee is approximately NPR 200–300. Bring a towel and flip-flops. The springs are open during daylight hours. Jhinu Danda teahouses are comfortable and a step up from higher altitude options. October evenings here are cool but pleasant.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Jhinu Danda/New Bridge back to Nayapul via Birethanti. The trail follows the Modi Khola river through lush subtropical vegetation, terraced farms, and small villages. Trek duration: 3–4 hours. Enjoy the contrast of lush lowland scenery after the high-altitude landscapes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Reach Nayapul and take a local bus or pre-arranged jeep back to Pokhara (approximately 1.5 hours). Return to Aegean Bliss Resort — enjoy a hot shower, fresh clothes, and the comfort of your resort accommodation. Rest and recover.
day_by_day.evening: Celebrate the completion of the Annapurna Base Camp trek with a special dinner at a quality restaurant in Pokhara. Visit the Lakeside area for a well-deserved treat — enjoy a cold drink (if desired) and reflect on the incredible week of trekking.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at Jhinu Danda teahouse before the final trek day
meals.lunch: Dal bhat or momos at Birethanti or Nayapul before the drive
meals.dinner: Celebration dinner at a mid-range Pokhara restaurant — try the Nepali set menu or continental options — approximately NPR 800–1,200

day_by_day.notes: Jeep from Nayapul to Pokhara costs approximately NPR 2,000–3,000 per vehicle (shared). Celebrate responsibly — your body is still recovering from altitude. Treat yourself to a massage in Pokhara — many excellent affordable options available on Lakeside Road (NPR 1,000–1,500 for a full body massage).

day_by_day.morning: Well-deserved rest morning at Aegean Bliss Resort. Sleep in, enjoy a leisurely breakfast, and use the resort facilities. If feeling energetic, take a gentle morning yoga session (many resorts and studios in Pokhara offer classes) or a light lakeside walk.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the International Mountain Museum in Pokhara — one of the finest mountaineering museums in the world, dedicated to the mountains of Nepal and the history of Himalayan exploration. Fascinating exhibits on Annapurna, Everest, and other 8,000m peaks. Entry fee approximately NPR 400.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Pokhara's Lakeside (Baidam) neighborhood — browse souvenir shops for handicrafts, Thangka paintings, prayer flags, and trekking mementos. Enjoy a sunset dinner at a lakeside restaurant with views of the Annapurna range reflected in Phewa Lake.

meals.breakfast: Full resort breakfast — treat yourself to eggs benedict or a continental spread
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the Mountain Museum café or a nearby bakery — try apple pie (Pokhara is famous for it) — approximately NPR 400–600
meals.dinner: Lakeside restaurant dinner — try Newari cuisine or wood-fired pizza for variety — approximately NPR 700–1,000

day_by_day.notes: The International Mountain Museum is approximately 3 km from Lakeside — take a taxi (NPR 200–300) or bicycle (rental approximately NPR 500/day). Today is a recovery day — prioritize rest and gentle activity. Rehydrate and eat nutritious meals to replenish after the trek.

day_by_day.morning: Take an early morning ultralight flight or helicopter tour over the Annapurna and Dhaulagiri ranges for a bird's-eye perspective of the mountains you just trekked through (optional, budget permitting — approximately USD 150–200 per person for a scenic flight). Alternatively, hike up to the World Peace Pagoda (Shanti Stupa) on the southern ridge above Phewa Lake for panoramic views — a 45-minute uphill hike from the lakeshore.
day_by_day.afternoon: Kayaking or paddleboarding on Phewa Lake — a fun and refreshing way to experience the lake with mountain reflections. Rent equipment from the lakeside (approximately NPR 300–500 per hour). Visit the Barahi Temple on an island in the middle of Phewa Lake by rowboat.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a traditional Nepali cultural show featuring Gurung, Magar, and Tharu folk dances and music at a local cultural center in Pokhara (approximately NPR 500–800). Return to the resort for a relaxed final evening in Pokhara.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast before the morning activity — banana pancakes and tea
meals.lunch: Lunch at a lakeside café after water activities — try local fish curry with rice — approximately NPR 500–700
meals.dinner: Traditional Nepali thali set at a cultural restaurant — approximately NPR 600–900

day_by_day.notes: The World Peace Pagoda hike is free and offers some of the best views in Pokhara — highly recommended. Bring water and sunscreen. Phewa Lake water activities are best in the morning when the lake is calm. Book the cultural show in advance through your resort or a local tour operator.

day_by_day.morning: Optional day trip to Sarangkot (1,592m) — the premier sunrise viewpoint near Pokhara, offering stunning panoramas of the Annapurna and Dhaulagiri ranges. Depart by taxi at 5:00 AM to reach the summit before sunrise. After sunrise, consider paragliding from Sarangkot — Pokhara is one of the world's top paragliding destinations (approximately USD 80–100 per person for a 30-minute tandem flight).
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Pokhara and visit the Gupteshwor Mahadev Cave — a sacred cave system near Davis Falls featuring underground river formations and a Shiva shrine. Explore the Devi's Fall (Patale Chhango) — a dramatic waterfall that disappears underground. Both sites are adjacent and entry costs approximately NPR 100–200.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Pokhara — enjoy a farewell dinner at your favorite restaurant discovered during the trip. Pack your bags and prepare for the journey back to Kathmandu the next day. Reflect on the incredible 13 days in the Annapurna region.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast before the early Sarangkot departure — energy bar and tea, or full breakfast upon return
meals.lunch: Lunch at a Pokhara restaurant after the cave visit — try Tibetan bread with butter and honey — approximately NPR 400–600
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at a quality Pokhara restaurant — splurge slightly on a special meal — approximately NPR 1,000–1,500

day_by_day.notes: Paragliding from Sarangkot is safe and well-regulated — book with a licensed operator (Sunrise Paragliding or Blue Sky Paragliding are reputable options). Flights typically last 30–45 minutes. Not recommended for those with heart conditions or severe fear of heights. Confirm your return transport to Kathmandu for Day 14.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in the Annapurna region. Enjoy a leisurely last breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort with views of the mountains. Take a final short walk along the lakeshore or resort grounds to soak in the last moments of the Himalayan landscape. Check out of the resort and arrange transport to Pokhara Airport or for the overland journey to Kathmandu.
day_by_day.afternoon: Travel from Pokhara to Kathmandu — either by domestic flight (25 minutes, approximately USD 80–120) or by tourist bus (approximately 6–7 hours, approximately NPR 1,000–1,500). If flying, arrive in Kathmandu with time to explore Thamel neighborhood for last-minute shopping — handicrafts, pashmina scarves, Thangka paintings, and trekking gear. If time permits, visit Swayambhunath (Monkey Temple) for a final Kathmandu cultural experience.
day_by_day.evening: Final dinner in Kathmandu at a quality restaurant in Thamel — try Krishnarpan restaurant for an authentic multi-course Nepali fine dining experience (NPR 2,000–3,000) or opt for a more casual dal bhat farewell meal. Head to the airport for your departure flight or rest at a Kathmandu hotel if departing the following day.

meals.breakfast: Full resort breakfast — make it special with fresh fruit, eggs, and good coffee
meals.lunch: Snack on the bus/plane or quick lunch in Kathmandu upon arrival — try a Thamel bakery for sandwiches and pastries — approximately NPR 400–600
meals.dinner: Farewell Kathmandu dinner — splurge on a memorable final meal — approximately NPR 1,500–3,000

day_by_day.notes: Domestic flights between Pokhara and Kathmandu are weather-dependent — have a backup plan (tourist bus) in case of cancellation. Allow extra time at Kathmandu airport for international departures. Bring any trekking gear you wish to donate — many local organizations accept used equipment. This concludes an extraordinary 14-day Annapurna adventure — a journey that will stay with you for a lifetime.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Annapurna, Nepal Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Poon Hill Sunrise Hike
experiences.description: Rise before dawn and hike to Poon Hill viewpoint at 3,210m for one of Nepal's most celebrated panoramic Himalayan sunrises, with golden light illuminating the Annapurna and Dhaulagiri ranges in a breathtaking 180-degree spectacle.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival & Rest — Flight UA lands at 22:30. No morning activities scheduled. Rest and recover from travel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrival & Rest — No afternoon activities scheduled prior to late-night arrival.
day_by_day.evening: Late-night arrival at Tribhuvan International Airport, Kathmandu. Private luxury transfer to your hotel in Pokhara or base lodge near Annapurna region. Welcome drink and late check-in at Aegean Bliss Resort. Brief orientation with your personal concierge.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in-flight or airport dining
meals.lunch: N/A — in-flight or airport dining
meals.dinner: Late-night welcome platter and herbal teas arranged by the resort upon arrival

day_by_day.notes: Ensure your resort is notified of the late 22:30 arrival. A private airport transfer should be pre-booked. Hydrate well and rest fully — altitude acclimatization begins tomorrow.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely late morning wake-up and full gourmet breakfast at the resort. Gentle acclimatization walk around the resort grounds and nearby lakeside (Phewa Lake if based in Pokhara). Meet your certified mountain guide for a detailed trek briefing and gear check.
day_by_day.afternoon: Scenic boat ride on Phewa Lake with views of the Annapurna and Machapuchare (Fishtail) mountain reflections. Visit the Tal Barahi Temple on the island. Explore the lakeside promenade at a relaxed pace. Optional visit to the International Mountain Museum for cultural and geographical context.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on the resort terrace with panoramic Himalayan views. Private welcome dinner curated by the resort's executive chef featuring Nepali and continental fusion cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet buffet breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort — fresh Himalayan honey, local breads, eggs to order, fresh juices
meals.lunch: Lakeside fine dining at Pokhara's top restaurant such as Moondance Restaurant or a private picnic arranged by the resort
meals.dinner: Private welcome dinner at Aegean Bliss Resort — multi-course Nepali fusion tasting menu with wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Day 2 is intentionally light to allow jet lag recovery and altitude acclimatization. Drink at least 3–4 liters of water. Avoid alcohol today if feeling the altitude.

day_by_day.morning: Early breakfast at the resort followed by a private luxury drive or helicopter transfer to Nayapul or Tikhedhunga — the gateway to the Annapurna foothills. Begin the first day of trekking through terraced rice paddies, rhododendron forests, and traditional Gurung villages on the route toward Ghorepani.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue trekking through the lush Modi Khola valley. Pass through Hile and Ulleri villages, climbing stone staircases surrounded by subtropical forest. Arrive at a premium teahouse lodge in Ulleri or Banthanti for afternoon rest. Enjoy a hot ginger-lemon tea and light snack on the lodge terrace.
day_by_day.evening: Settle into your pre-booked luxury lodge accommodation. Enjoy a hot shower and change of clothes. Sunset views over the valley. Dinner at the lodge followed by an evening briefing from your guide about the next day's route.

meals.breakfast: Full hot breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort before departure — porridge, eggs, toast, fresh fruit
meals.lunch: Packed gourmet lunch box prepared by the resort or a hearty dal bhat at a quality teahouse en route
meals.dinner: Premium teahouse dinner — Nepali set meal with lentil soup, rice, seasonal vegetables, and yak cheese

day_by_day.notes: Trek distance today is approximately 8–10 km with significant elevation gain. Trekking poles are highly recommended. Your guide will manage the pace carefully. Luxury porter service is included — you carry only a daypack.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning start after a hot breakfast. Continue trekking through dense rhododendron and oak forests toward Ghorepani (2,860m). The trail offers increasingly dramatic mountain vistas as you ascend. Arrive at Ghorepani by late morning and check into your premium lodge.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rest and acclimatize at Ghorepani. Optional short exploratory hike around the village to stretch legs and soak in the alpine atmosphere. Visit the local monastery or interact with Magar and Gurung community members. Enjoy a traditional butter tea or hot chocolate at the lodge.
day_by_day.evening: Stunning sunset views of Dhaulagiri, Annapurna South, and Hiunchuli from Ghorepani. Early dinner and early bedtime — a 04:00 wake-up call is scheduled for the Poon Hill sunrise hike tomorrow. Guide will brief you on the pre-dawn hike.

meals.breakfast: Hot porridge, eggs, toast, and Nepali milk tea at the teahouse lodge
meals.lunch: Teahouse lunch at Ghorepani — vegetable noodle soup, momos (dumplings), and fresh juice
meals.dinner: Hearty teahouse dinner — pasta, vegetable curry, or Nepali dal bhat with apple pie dessert

day_by_day.notes: Ghorepani sits at 2,860m. Stay well-hydrated and avoid overexertion this afternoon. Altitude headaches are common — Diamox may be considered if prescribed. Layers of warm clothing are essential for the cold evening.

day_by_day.morning: POON HILL SUNRISE HIKE — Wake at 04:00 for the iconic pre-dawn ascent to Poon Hill (3,210m). Hike by headlamp through the silent forest for approximately 45–60 minutes. Witness one of Nepal's most celebrated panoramic sunrises — a 180-degree arc of Himalayan giants including Dhaulagiri, Annapurna I, Annapurna South, Hiunchuli, Machapuchare, and Gangapurna bathed in golden alpenglow. Photography session with your guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend back to Ghorepani for a well-earned hot breakfast. Begin trekking toward Tadapani through spectacular rhododendron forests — among the largest in the world. The trail offers continuous mountain views and diverse birdlife. Arrive at Tadapani (2,630m) and settle into your lodge.
day_by_day.evening: Relax on the Tadapani lodge terrace with unobstructed views of Annapurna and Machapuchare. Enjoy a therapeutic hot stone foot soak arranged by your premium lodge. Dinner by candlelight with mountain silhouettes at dusk.

meals.breakfast: Light snack and thermos of hot tea before the Poon Hill hike; full hot breakfast upon return to Ghorepani
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or teahouse stop en route to Tadapani
meals.dinner: Premium teahouse dinner at Tadapani — roasted potatoes, vegetable curry, Himalayan cheese board, and hot chocolate

day_by_day.notes: Poon Hill is the highlight of the entire itinerary. October offers crystal-clear skies with excellent visibility. Bring all camera equipment, extra batteries (cold drains them fast), and warm layers — temperatures at 04:00 can drop below 0°C.

day_by_day.morning: Morning meditation or yoga session on the lodge terrace at sunrise (optional, guide can arrange). Post-breakfast trek from Tadapani descending through bamboo and rhododendron forest toward Chhomrong (2,170m) — the gateway village to the Annapurna Sanctuary. The trail passes through Gurung villages with traditional stone architecture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Chhomrong and check into your premium lodge. Explore the charming terraced village. Visit a local Gurung family home for a cultural immersion experience arranged by your guide. Enjoy spectacular close-up views of Annapurna South and Hiunchuli directly above the village.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset drinks on the Chhomrong lodge terrace — one of the most dramatic viewpoints on the entire circuit. Dinner featuring local Gurung specialties. Evening star-gazing session with your guide identifying Himalayan constellations in the pollution-free sky.

meals.breakfast: Full hot breakfast at Tadapani lodge — eggs, toast, granola, and fresh ginger tea
meals.lunch: Teahouse lunch en route — vegetable soup, fried rice, and fresh lemonade
meals.dinner: Gurung cultural dinner at Chhomrong — gundruk soup, dhido (buckwheat porridge), local vegetables, and raksi (local millet spirit) tasting

day_by_day.notes: The descent to Chhomrong involves significant stone staircase sections — trekking poles and careful footing are advised. This village marks the boundary of the Annapurna Conservation Area inner zone.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and rejuvenation day at Chhomrong. Enjoy a slow morning with extended breakfast and mountain views. Optional short hike to Chomrong Khola (river) and back for a gentle morning stretch. In-room or terrace massage arranged by your concierge using local herbal oils.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cultural workshop — traditional Nepali cooking class with a local family, learning to prepare dal bhat, momos, and sel roti (rice donuts). Visit the local monastery and interact with resident monks. Photography walk through the village's terraced fields.
day_by_day.evening: Private bonfire evening at the lodge (if permitted and weather allows). Storytelling session with your mountain guide about Himalayan legends, Gurung culture, and personal summit stories. Premium dinner with a curated selection of Himalayan herbal teas.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely gourmet breakfast — pancakes with local honey, fresh fruit, Nepali tea ceremony
meals.lunch: Dishes prepared during the cooking class — authentic and freshly made
meals.dinner: Premium lodge dinner — continental and Nepali fusion, yak steak or trout, local vegetable sides, and dessert

day_by_day.notes: Day 7 is a planned rest day to prevent trekker's fatigue and maintain acclimatization. This is ideal for mid-trip recovery. Ensure gear is dried, cleaned, and repacked for the next trekking days.

day_by_day.morning: Early breakfast and begin the dramatic descent and ascent trek from Chhomrong toward Dovan (2,600m), passing through Sinuwa and the Bamboo zone. The trail enters the inner Annapurna Sanctuary corridor — a sacred glacial valley enclosed by some of the world's highest peaks. Lush bamboo forests give way to alpine terrain.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue trekking through Himalaya (2,920m) toward Deurali (3,230m). The landscape becomes increasingly raw and dramatic — towering canyon walls, glacial rivers, and the first views of the Sanctuary's inner peaks. Arrive at Deurali lodge and rest.
day_by_day.evening: The temperature drops significantly at this altitude. Warm up with hot soup and tea by the lodge fire. Dinner and early rest in preparation for the high-altitude push to Annapurna Base Camp tomorrow.

meals.breakfast: Hot porridge, boiled eggs, toast, and Nepali tea at Chhomrong
meals.lunch: Teahouse lunch at Himalaya — garlic soup (excellent for altitude), fried noodles, and hot lemon
meals.dinner: Hearty lodge dinner at Deurali — pasta, vegetable curry, and hot chocolate with marshmallows

day_by_day.notes: Garlic soup is strongly recommended from this point onward — it is a traditional Himalayan remedy for altitude sickness. The trail through the Sanctuary corridor can be affected by avalanche debris — always follow your guide's instructions.

day_by_day.morning: The most spectacular day of the trek — early morning push from Deurali to Annapurna Base Camp (ABC) at 4,130m. Trek through Machhapuchhre Base Camp (MBC) at 3,700m with awe-inspiring views of the sacred Fishtail peak (Machapuchare). The final ascent to ABC opens into a breathtaking glacial amphitheater encircled by Annapurna I (8,091m), Annapurna South, Gangapurna, Hiunchuli, and Machapuchare.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Annapurna Base Camp — a profound achievement. Spend the afternoon exploring the base camp area, visiting the memorial chortens, and absorbing the overwhelming 360-degree Himalayan panorama. Photography session in the golden afternoon light. Rest and acclimatize at your premium lodge.
day_by_day.evening: Magical evening at 4,130m — watch the peaks glow in alpenglow shades of pink and orange as the sun sets. Celebrate your arrival with a special dinner. Clear October skies offer extraordinary star-gazing — the Milky Way is visible in full brilliance above the Himalayan giants.

meals.breakfast: Early hot breakfast at Deurali — porridge, eggs, toast before the final push
meals.lunch: Hot soup and snacks at Machhapuchhre Base Camp teahouse
meals.dinner: Celebratory dinner at ABC lodge — best available menu including pasta, soup, hot drinks, and a special dessert to mark the achievement

day_by_day.notes: Annapurna Base Camp at 4,130m is the highest point of this itinerary. Altitude sickness symptoms must be taken seriously — descend immediately if severe headache, vomiting, or disorientation occurs. October is one of the best months for ABC with stable weather and clear skies.

day_by_day.morning: Wake before dawn for the ABC sunrise — arguably the most dramatic mountain sunrise in the Himalayas. Watch Annapurna I and its neighbors ignite in shades of crimson and gold as the first light hits the glaciers. Extended photography and meditation session at the base camp. Farewell to the Sanctuary.
day_by_day.afternoon: Begin the descent from ABC back through MBC, Deurali, and Himalaya toward Bamboo (2,310m). The descent is significantly faster but requires careful footing on steep sections. The changing vegetation zones — from glacial to bamboo to subtropical — unfold in reverse.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Bamboo lodge, dramatically lower in altitude and noticeably warmer. Enjoy the relief of lower altitude with a hearty dinner. Celebrate the successful ABC trek with your guide and porter team.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at ABC before descent — tea, biscuits, and energy bars
meals.lunch: Teahouse lunch at Himalaya or Deurali — hot soup, fried rice, and fresh lemon tea
meals.dinner: Warm lodge dinner at Bamboo — dal bhat, vegetable curry, and fresh salad

day_by_day.notes: The descent from 4,130m to 2,310m in one day is demanding on the knees — trekking poles are essential. Pace yourself and take breaks. The increased oxygen at lower altitude will feel remarkably refreshing.

day_by_day.morning: Morning trek from Bamboo back through Sinuwa and up to Chhomrong. The familiar trail feels different on the return — notice details missed on the way up. Arrive at Chhomrong for a mid-morning break with tea and snacks at your favorite lodge.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue trekking from Chhomrong down to Jhinu Danda (1,780m). The reward here is the famous Jhinu Danda natural hot spring — a geothermal pool beside the Modi Khola river. Soak your tired trekking muscles in the steaming mineral-rich waters with views of the surrounding forested hills.
day_by_day.evening: Settle into the premium Jhinu Danda lodge. Enjoy a therapeutic massage if available. Celebrate the near-completion of the trek with a special dinner. Reflect on the journey with your guide over evening tea.

meals.breakfast: Full hot breakfast at Bamboo lodge before departure
meals.lunch: Teahouse lunch at Chhomrong — momos, soup, and fresh juice
meals.dinner: Premium dinner at Jhinu Danda lodge — grilled vegetables, pasta, local cheese, and herbal tea

day_by_day.notes: The Jhinu Danda hot springs are a legendary trekker's reward and should not be missed. Bring a towel and swimwear. The springs are most enjoyable in the late afternoon before sunset.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning trek from Jhinu Danda down through New Bridge and along the Modi Khola river valley to Nayapul. The trail winds through terraced farmland, suspension bridges, and riverside forests. Arrive at Nayapul to meet your private luxury vehicle.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury transfer back to Pokhara (approximately 1.5–2 hours). Arrive at Aegean Bliss Resort for a triumphant return. Hot bath, premium room service, and full resort facilities await. Enjoy a long, indulgent shower and change into fresh clothes — a moment of pure luxury after 10 days of trekking.
day_by_day.evening: Celebratory dinner at Pokhara's finest restaurant — a premium multi-course meal with wine pairing to mark the completion of the Annapurna trek. Lakeside stroll under the stars with views of the illuminated Machapuchare reflection on Phewa Lake.

meals.breakfast: Hot breakfast at Jhinu Danda lodge before the final trek
meals.lunch: Celebratory lunch at a quality Pokhara restaurant upon return — international cuisine, fresh salads, and cold beverages
meals.dinner: Premium celebratory dinner at Pokhara's top fine dining venue — multi-course tasting menu, wine or cocktail pairing, and dessert

day_by_day.notes: This is a landmark day — the completion of the Annapurna Sanctuary Trek. Tip your guide and porter team generously today as a gesture of appreciation for their exceptional service throughout the journey.

day_by_day.morning: Full luxury resort day. Sleep in and enjoy an extended breakfast on your private terrace or at the resort restaurant. Full-day access to resort spa — book a 90-minute deep tissue or Ayurvedic massage, steam bath, and hydrotherapy session to fully restore post-trek muscles.
day_by_day.afternoon: Optional scenic helicopter flight over the Annapurna range for a bird's-eye perspective of the terrain you just trekked (bookable through the resort concierge — a truly extraordinary premium experience). Alternatively, enjoy a private yoga and stretching session with a resort instructor, followed by leisure time at the resort pool.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktail hour at the resort's premium bar with panoramic mountain views. Private chef's table dinner experience — a bespoke menu designed around your preferences, served in an exclusive setting at the resort.

meals.breakfast: Extended gourmet breakfast at the resort — eggs Benedict, smoked salmon, fresh pastries, fruit platters, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Light poolside lunch — fresh salads, club sandwiches, fresh juices, and smoothies
meals.dinner: Private chef's table dinner at Aegean Bliss Resort — bespoke 6-course tasting menu with Himalayan ingredients and international wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: The helicopter flight over Annapurna must be booked in advance through the resort concierge and is subject to weather conditions. October typically offers excellent flying weather. This experience provides an unparalleled aerial perspective of the entire route you trekked.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Nepal. Leisurely breakfast at the resort. Pack and prepare for departure. Last lakeside walk along Phewa Lake to collect final memories and photographs of the Annapurna range. Purchase premium Nepali souvenirs — pashmina shawls, thangka paintings, hand-carved Himalayan items — from curated shops recommended by your concierge.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury transfer to Pokhara Airport for the short domestic flight back to Kathmandu, or direct road transfer depending on onward flight schedule. If time permits, a brief stop at Kathmandu's Thamel district for last-minute premium shopping or a visit to Boudhanath Stupa — a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Tribhuvan International Airport, Kathmandu. Final Nepali meal at the premium airport lounge or a Kathmandu restaurant en route — a fitting farewell to one of the world's most extraordinary destinations.

meals.lunch: Premium restaurant in Kathmandu or airport lounge dining — continental or Nepali cuisine

day_by_day.notes: Confirm all departure logistics with the resort concierge 24 hours in advance.
